I farm in Quzhou County, Hebei, so at the start of the season I will keep to the cropping pattern I trust most on the North China Plain: winter wheat followed by summer maize on most of my land. That system fits my weather, my irrigation conditions, and my age because I already know how to manage it and it spreads income across the year. I do not want to take big risks on unfamiliar cash crops. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and stability, but I will keep management simple and practical. For wheat, I will control fertilizer, give a few irrigations at the key stages, and spray only when disease or insects are likely to reduce yield. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize, use hybrid seed, apply enough fertilizer for strong growth, irrigate when needed, and keep weed and pest pressure under control. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for me than deep ploughing every time, and it fits the wheat-maize double-cropping schedule.
